correctness.rationale: The theorem supplies the exact N-by-N matrix, full assumptions and proof. Invertibility over formal series follows from Q(0)=-product of strictly positive p_j(0); kernel rows cancel all nonunit simple zeros, the last row cancels the value at 1, and Q'(1) equals the strictly positive mean-drift gap. Exponential moments make all reconstructed phase functions analytic on a disk of radius larger than one, hence finite complex signed measures. The coefficient at zero equals each boundary component. The generating-function equations are precisely reflected Lindley transitions. Negative mean N-step drift and positive zero-claim probabilities give a unique recurrent stationary class; Cesaro ergodicity forces any finite zero-mass invariant signed measure to vanish. A standalone exact-rational script reproduces a nontrivial two-season matrix of determinant 1. The infinite theorem is supported by the proof, not by extrapolation from the finite test.

value.rationale: The matrix is the necessary input to computing the initial phase probabilities and hence ultimate survival probabilities for general N-seasonal unit-premium risk models. Its nonsingularity had been left as an explicit open issue, despite detailed prior computational evidence, so a general light-tail theorem supplies a new structural guarantee for an infinite family of seasonal distributions and arbitrary period N. The signed-invariant-measure mechanism also explains why spectral pole cancellation suffices for unique boundary data. This is neither a fixed numerical recomputation nor a merely formal restatement of published recurrence equations.
